title: Two Quiet Hiders: N and S
kidRule: Two letters love to hide! N stays quiet right after M at the end of a word, as in AUTUMN. S stays quiet in a few special words, as in ISLAND. We write them, but we never say them!
hint: A quiet letter is hiding in this word. It is an N right after an M, or an S that you cannot hear. Which one is it, and where does it go?
reminder: A quiet letter hides here: an N right after the M (M-N), or a silent S.

check.question: Why can't we hear the N in AUTUMN?
check.correctAnswer: N stays quiet when it comes right after M at the end of a word!
distractors: Because the letter U makes every N quiet
Because words about the seasons never say their last letter

words.def: The season between summer and winter, when leaves change color and drop from the trees.
words.sent: In autumn we rake the leaves into a big pile.
words.story: Leaves look green because of a green material called chlorophyll. In autumn the green fades away, and the yellow and orange that were hiding underneath finally show!
words.card: Every *autumn* my *tum*my is full of pumpkin pie!

words.def: A piece of land with water all around it.
words.sent: We rowed the boat out to a tiny island in the lake.
words.story: For hundreds of years this word was spelled with no S at all. People added the S later because they mixed it up with the word 'isle', but nobody ever said it out loud!
words.card: An *island* is *land* where the crabs wear tiny sunglasses!

words.def: A tall, round post that holds up part of a building, or a straight up-and-down line of things.
words.sent: A stone column stood on each side of the door.
words.story: The Parthenon, a famous temple in Greece, was built with 46 big columns around the outside more than 2,400 years ago, and many of them still stand today!
words.card: A *col*d penguin hugged the *column* and got stuck like a popsicle!

words.def: A song that people sing to give praise or thanks.
words.sent: The choir sang a gentle hymn at the start of the service.
words.story: The word comes from the Greek word 'hymnos', which meant a song of praise!
words.card: The s*hy* frog sang a *hymn* so softly that only the snails heard it!

words.def: A path to walk along between rows of seats or shelves.
words.sent: The cereal is in the third aisle of the store.
words.story: The word comes from the Latin 'ala', which means wing, because the first aisles were the side wings of big churches!
words.card: The sn*ai*l took all day to slide down the grocery *aisle*!

words.def: An island, usually a small one. This word is used mostly in stories, poems, and the names of places.
words.sent: The pirates buried their treasure on a sandy isle.
words.story: The Isle of Man, in the sea between England and Ireland, is the home of the Manx cat, a cat that often has no tail!
words.card: This *isle* *is* so small that the crab and the coconut have to take turns!

words.def: Very serious and quiet, with no joking.
words.sent: The knights made a solemn promise to protect the castle.
words.story: The guards outside Buckingham Palace in London are famous for keeping a solemn face, even when visitors try to make them laugh!
words.card: The *sole* of my shoe made a rude squeak during the *solemn* song!

words.sent: A single palm tree grew on the tiny islet.
words.story: The Maldives, a country in the Indian Ocean, is made up of about 1,200 small islands and islets!
words.card: *Let* me off! This *islet* only has room for one flamingo and me!

words.def: Broken bits and pieces left lying around after something breaks or a storm passes.
words.sent: After the windy night, we cleared the debris from the yard.
words.story: Thousands of pieces of space debris, like old satellites and rocket parts, are circling the Earth right now, and scientists keep track of them!
words.card: The *debris* from my *bri*ck tower covered the whole rug!

words.def: To say very strongly that something is wrong or bad.
words.sent: People all around the world condemn dumping trash in the ocean.
words.story: Say the cousin word 'condemnation' and you can hear the hiding N loud and clear!
words.card: The cats *condemn* the dog for eating all the ba*con*!
